source.title: Understanding the Generalization Benefits of Late Learning Rate Decay
source.authors: Yinuo Ren; Chao Ma; Le-Xing Ying

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10 VGG-11 learning-rate schedule results on held-out test loss, a conceptual test of how an optimizer/training schedule affects generalization.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported VGG-11 test-loss outcomes under different learning-rate decay timings and the corresponding training-loss behavior. The Gaussian reparameterized model results are theoretical analyses, not empirical network findings. Cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate decay timing, which none of V1–V8 names. Its own results do not compare random versus natural labels, widths, architectures, optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Generalization results alone do not establish a test of these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report better final generalization with later learning-rate decay in their VGG-11 experiment and offer a continuous-time analysis of a nonlinear reparameterized regression model in which extended large-learning-rate dynamics approach a minimum-norm training solution. Near-optimal generalization is conditional on assumptions, rather than established generally for neural networks.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical schedule uses SGD with a prolonged initial learning rate followed by decay, but the study does not test random-label memorization or the versions' specified comparisons. The analytical model uses continuous-time SDE dynamics and a nonlinear reparameterization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported final testing loss varies with the timing of learning-rate decay; training loss changes little across decay timings once it stabilizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For VGG-11 on CIFAR-10 with SGD and batch size 128, later decay from learning rate 0.1 to 0.01 yields lower final test loss after 1000 additional epochs; subsequent training loss depends little on decay timing after stabilization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extending the initial large-learning-rate phase can improve final test loss despite similar subsequent training loss in this setup, with total training duration varying across decay timings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2024
record.problems: The empirical evidence described here is one VGG-11 image-classification setup and is presented qualitatively; no numerical test-loss values, uncertainty estimates, or controls are stated. The paper notes that its theoretical analysis is continuous-time and leaves discrete-time analysis for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported empirical findings. The theoretical model and cited results are not catalog rows for empirical network conditions in the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and their coexistence under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation or weight-decay settings.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and its ranking performance relative to norm and margin measures. PCA landscape visualizations and theoretical curvature arguments do not test these comparisons.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's discussion of flat minima and SGD does not supply a magnitude-aware sharpness test or an adaptive-optimizer comparison. No verdict labels apply to V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label coexistence comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

rows.subject: VGG-11
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained along the main path with SGD at learning rate 0.1 for 1000 epochs.
rows.value: Training loss stabilizes after the initial ∼500 epochs.
rows.note: The paper describes this as the main path; no numerical loss value is given.
rows.check: The reported training-loss stabilization is accurate, but measures no listed version. Its observed state cannot be interpreted as observing a version's effect.

rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Subpaths started at different epochs of the main path and continued for 1000 epochs after reducing the learning rate to 0.01.

conditions.value: varies; additional subpaths start from epoch 200 onward

rows.value: Delaying the reduction in learning rate results in a lower final testing loss.
rows.note: The source gives a qualitative trend, not separate numeric values for each decay time.
rows.check: The qualitative test-loss trend is accurately reported, but learning-rate decay timing measures no listed version. Later decay also entails more total training because every subpath receives another 1000 epochs.

rows.value: The timing of the learning rate decay has a small impact on the subsequent training phase; the pattern appears chaotic after training loss stabilizes.

rows.check: The small dependence of subsequent training loss on decay timing is accurately reported, but does not demonstrate a partial effect for any listed version.
